cards.info: What is the formula for calculating the range of a data set?
cards.backInfo: The range is calculated by subtracting the minimum value from the maximum value ($Range = Max - Min$).

cards.info: What is the formula for the interquartile range (IQR)?
cards.backInfo: The interquartile range is calculated by subtracting the first quartile from the third quartile ($IQR = Q3 - Q1$).

cards.info: What does standard deviation represent conceptually?
cards.backInfo: Standard deviation represents the typical or average distance of data points from the mean of the data set.

cards.info: Why is the range considered highly sensitive to outliers?
cards.backInfo: The range is sensitive because it depends entirely on the two most extreme values in the data set.

cards.info: Why is the interquartile range (IQR) resistant to outliers?
cards.backInfo: The IQR is resistant because it only measures the spread of the middle 50% of the data.

cards.info: How do outliers affect the standard deviation of a data set?
cards.backInfo: Standard deviation increases when outliers are added because those points are located far from the mean.

cards.info: Which measure of spread should be used to ignore extreme values?
cards.backInfo: The interquartile range (IQR) is the appropriate measure when you need to ignore extreme values.
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A flowchart showing how to choose between Range, IQR, and Standard Deviation based on the presence of outliers.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/7d9ebe41-1fad-4501-8792-08a6d6371d21-1786506112667-368.webp)

cards.info: What specific portion of a distribution does the IQR describe?
cards.backInfo: The interquartile range (IQR) specifically describes the spread of the middle 50% of a distribution.

cards.info: Is standard deviation a robust measure against extreme values?
cards.backInfo: No, it is a mistake to assume robustness; standard deviation is actually sensitive to extreme values.

cards.info: What happens to range and SD if a much higher maximum is added?
cards.backInfo: Adding a new maximum value much higher than the previous one will increase both the range and standard deviation.

cards.info: If a data set spans from 5 to 100, what is its range?
cards.backInfo: The range is 95, calculated by subtracting the minimum (5) from the maximum (100).

cards.info: In a box plot, what distance does the width of the box represent?
cards.backInfo: The width of the box represents the Interquartile Range (IQR), calculated as $Q3 - Q1$.

cards.info: Which measure accounts for every data point's position relative to the average?
cards.backInfo: Standard Deviation (SD) accounts for the position of every single data point relative to the mean.

cards.info: Which measure of spread is most affected by a single extreme outlier?
cards.backInfo: The Range is most affected because it is determined solely by the maximum and minimum values.

cards.info: Why does the IQR remain unchanged if the maximum value increases significantly?
cards.backInfo: The IQR is robust because it only considers the middle 50% and ignores the tails.

cards.info: Why does adding a value far from the mean increase Standard Deviation?
cards.backInfo: Standard Deviation increases because it averages the distance of all points, including outliers, from the mean.

cards.info: When data is skewed, why is IQR preferred over Range for spread?
cards.backInfo: IQR is preferred because it describes the 'typical' data spread while ignoring skewed tails or extremes.
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A flowchart showing how to choose between Range, IQR, and Standard Deviation based on the presence of outliers.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/7d9ebe41-1fad-4501-8792-08a6d6371d21-1786506112667-368.webp)

cards.info: What percentage of data is contained within the Interquartile Range?
cards.backInfo: The Interquartile Range (IQR) contains exactly the middle 50% of the data points.

cards.info: Given Min=5, Q1=15, Med=20, Q3=30, Max=100, what is the IQR?
cards.backInfo: The IQR is 15, calculated by subtracting Q1 (15) from Q3 (30).

cards.info: True or False: Standard Deviation is resistant to extreme values.
cards.backInfo: False. Standard Deviation is sensitive to outliers because every data point is used in its calculation.
